title: Pairwise Sample Complexity for Fair Active Ranking with Cascaded Norm Objectives

problem.claim: Pairwise-comparison ranking systems need to address fairness while constructing rankings through active preference queries.

gap.claim: Fairness concerns are largely unaddressed in active ranking frameworks.

contributions.claim: A fairness-aware active ranking approach adaptively queries pairwise preferences to construct rankings that are probably approximately correct and fair.
A flexible cascaded norm-based objective balances error distribution within and across socially salient groups and unifies fairness objectives.
Group-blind and group-aware algorithms are developed with derived sample complexity bounds.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their fairness-aware active ranking approach as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical evaluations on COMPAS and German Credit report reduced sample complexity and fairer rankings.
The authors report theoretical insights and practical methods for improving fairness and reliability in active ranking systems.

narrative_sequence.summary: Pairwise-comparison ranking systems have fairness concerns, especially in active ranking.
The work introduces fairness-aware adaptive pairwise querying and a cascaded norm-based objective.
The objective unifies equal-error and proportionate-error fairness concepts.
Group-blind and group-aware algorithms are paired with sample complexity bounds.
Experiments on two real-world datasets report efficiency and fairer rankings, with applications including hiring and recommendations.

source_observation.claim: A cascaded norm-based objective can balance error distribution within and across socially salient groups.

interpretation.claim: Fairness objectives may be treated as configurable points within a shared error-distribution framework.

application.claim: Ranking systems can evaluate alternative fairness criteria through a unified objective design.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when one fairness criterion should be preferred over another.

source_observation.claim: Group-blind and group-aware algorithms are developed with sample complexity bounds.

interpretation.claim: Fair active ranking may require distinct algorithmic treatments depending on group-information availability.

application.claim: System designers can compare group-blind and group-aware approaches when selecting a fair ranking procedure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not report the assumptions or conditions underlying the sample complexity bounds.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal fairness definitions or cascaded norm formulation.
The abstract does not provide numerical sample complexity bounds or evaluation results.
The abstract does not describe dataset splits, baselines, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported findings.
